title: Fibonacci Sequence
story: Fibonacci numbers appear everywhere in nature: flower petals, pinecone spirals, rabbit populations. The sequence starts 0, 1 and each next number is the sum of the previous two. Generate this beautiful, ubiquitous sequence.
why: Fibonacci generation teaches iterative accumulation — a fundamental pattern where each step depends on previous results, perfect for while loops and Vec.
analogy: Fibonacci numbers are like a growing snowball rolling downhill — each new layer is the size of the previous two combined. The snowball starts tiny (0, 1) but grows exponentially. Your program tracks its growth at every step.
try_it: Find the first Fibonacci number greater than 1 million. Calculate the ratio F(n+1)/F(n) for n=10, 20, 30 and see how it approaches the golden ratio. Try generating 50 terms — when do the numbers get too large for Int?
tips: Iterative is always faster than recursive for Fibonacci
Store previous two values (a, b) and update: (a, b) = (b, a+b)
Start with base cases: push 0 and 1 separately before the loop
common_mistakes: Using recursion for large n — it's exponentially slow
Starting indices wrong: F(0)=0, F(1)=1, not F(0)=1, F(1)=1
Forgetting to handle count=0 or count=1 edge cases separately
